land.text: Tailevu and Naitasiri (with Bau island) and Lomaiviti, the Kubuna provinces of the Kubuna page read back into the 1850s-60s: a 35 km circle at 178.45 E, 17.75 S for Tailevu and Naitasiri (10 land cells, about 2,530 km2 at the grid, against 955 km2 for Tailevu and 1,666 km2 for Naitasiri on their pages) and a 60 km circle at 179.1 E, 17.75 S for Lomaiviti (Ovalau, Gau, Koro, Nairai). Natural Earth's Central Division is not used: it also holds Rewa, Namosi and Serua

predecessors.note: The Cakobau page: Chairman of the Confederacy of Independent Kingdoms of Viti 8 May 1865 - 2 May 1867, then 'Tui Bau (King of Bau) 2 May 1867 - 1869', then Tui Viti from 5 June 1871. Bau's own dossier (kingdom-of-bau) is written by this group.

land.text: Ma'afu's Tovata, 'covering most of northern and eastern Fiji' (Lau, Cakaudrove, Bua, Macuata)

predecessors.note: The Kingdom of Fiji page says the kingdom covered all of Fiji except Rotuma and that Ma'afu signed the Deed of Cession as one of its chiefs in 1874; neither page dates the Tovata's entry into the kingdom, taken here as the June 1871 proclamation at confidence 1.

land.text: the whole kingdom, ceded by the Deed of Cession of 10 October 1874 and organised as the Colony of Fiji

successors.note: The Colony of Fiji (1874-1970) has no Cliopatria row of its own; it sits inside the British Colonial Empire row. Rotuma joined the colony separately in 1881 (not on these pages).

capitals.name: Levuka (Ovalau)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Levuka; 'the Legislative Assembly met for the first time in Levuka in November 1871'. Coordinates approximate (the page gives none).

keyframe_review.note: The page gives the kingdom's territory as all of modern Fiji except Rotuma, which is what the shape draws (Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Lau, Lomaiviti, Kadavu; bbox 177.1-179.9 E, 16.2-19.1 S). No infobox area; Cliopatria's 21,696 km2 against Fiji's land area of about 18,300 km2 is within a factor of two (reef and lagoon padding). Known problem: Cliopatria files the row under South America; the geometry itself is in Fiji. Effective control of the Viti Levu interior (the Kai Colo) is not addressed by the page; the shape is kept whole.

correction.text: the kingdom unchanged ('all of modern Fiji except Rotuma'); only the years change: 1873-1874, not 1873-1876

keyframe_review.note: The kingdom ended with the Deed of Cession on 10 October 1874 ('Cakobau, Ma'afu, and several senior chiefs signed two copies of the Deed of Cession, establishing the Colony of Fiji'); 1875-1876 belong to the Colony of Fiji (British Colonial Empire), not to this state. The shape itself is identical to the 1871 shape.

ledger.note: 1871: Cakobau is proclaimed Tui Viti, King of Fiji, at Levuka. Infobox 'Established: 5 June 1871'; 'John Bates Thurston, the British honorary consul, persuaded the chiefs to accept a constitutional monarchy with Cakobau as king', with 'real power given to a cabinet and legislature dominated by Australian settlers'. The core is Cakobau's Bau; the page describes the kingdom's claimed extent, not what it held in June 1871.

region.text: Ma'afu's Tovata: 'most of northern and eastern Fiji'

ledger.note: 1871: Ma'afu's northern and eastern confederacy comes under the Fijian crown. Bridging event: the Kingdom of Fiji page says the kingdom covered 'all of modern Fiji except Rotuma' and that Ma'afu signed the 1874 cession as one of its chiefs, but neither it nor the Ma'afu page dates his adhesion; 'Cakobau and his rival Ma'afu vacillated for many months over their power' in 1872-1874.

1874: Fiji is ceded to Britain. 'Cakobau, Ma'afu, and several senior chiefs signed two copies of the Deed of Cession, establishing the Colony of Fiji' on 10 October 1874, after Cakobau's 'final offer' of 21 March 1874 and the arrival of Sir Hercules Robinson on HMS Dido on 23 September 1874. Cakobau page: 'He gave his war club to Queen Victoria on 10 October 1874 when the Deed of Cession' was signed.

certainty.note: An island kingdom: the coasts are sharp, but the kingdom's writ in the Viti Levu highlands and the standing of Ma'afu's north and east were unsettled throughout; no treaty or survey line existed before the cession.

sources.title: Kingdom of Fiji
sources.note: Identity, 5 June 1871, Levuka, the 1872-1874 cession offers, the Deed of Cession of 10 October 1874, extent 'all of modern Fiji except Rotuma'.

sources.title: Seru Epenisa Cakobau
sources.note: Vunivalu of Bau from 8 December 1852; Confederacy of Viti 1865-1867; Tui Bau 1867-1869; Tui Viti 5 June 1871 - 10 October 1874; death 1 February 1883.

sources.title: Enele Ma'afu
sources.note: The Tovata Confederacy of 1867 'covering most of northern and eastern Fiji'; Tui Lau February 1869; Tonga's disclaimer of sovereignty 1868; the 1874 cession.

notes: Cliopatria's row ends in 1876; the state ended with the Deed of Cession on 10 October 1874 (keyframe 1873 adjusted to 1873-1874). The row is filed by Cliopatria under South America (data/README known problem); the geometry is in Fiji and is kept. Predecessors: this group writes kingdom-of-bau and tovata-confederacy (states Cliopatria lacks) as the two Fijian confederations that the 1871 kingdom joined; the date of Ma'afu's adhesion is not given by any page opened and is bridged at confidence 1. Successor: the Colony of Fiji has no Cliopatria row and is counted in british-colonial-empire. The Kai Colo (highland Viti Levu) wars of 1873 and the interior's independence from Bau are not on the pages opened and are left to a gap-filler. Levuka's coordinates are approximate (no page opened gives them). Review repair of 2026-10-18: the land handed over by kingdom-of-bau (identity/predecessors/0) is now Tailevu and Naitasiri (35 km circle at 178.45 E, 17.75 S) plus Lomaiviti (60 km circle at 179.1 E, 17.75 S), the same as kingdom-of-bau's dissolve land, instead of Natural Earth's Central Division, which also holds Rewa, Namosi and Serua.
